correctness_confidence.basis: By hand I re-derived: polar form (2), L_fP formula, threshold minimisation at c=a^{1/3} giving (1+a^{2/3})^{3/2}, pairing (8)-(9), the cancellation and h_c(0)=1 in Lemma 3, boundary signs, and the Prop. 4 arithmetic. All consistent. Not checked: Fejer-Riesz citation in [1], numerics, any machine check.

rigor.basis: Necessity and sufficiency are explicit and quantitative, and the paper states what it does not prove (no sharp degree rate, omega=0, mixed harmonics). Weak points: boundary regularity of h_c (orders 1/2, 3/2) is sketched tersely; the extension to k>1 and to d sin2θ is only outlined; the Section 6 limit argument is short.

novelty.basis: An exact certificate threshold for the Liu-Fitzsimmons family is a natural refinement of a one-month-old counterexample. The tools (Fejer-Riesz, harmonic conjugates, Poisson smoothing) are classical. I could not check priority beyond the arXiv abstract of [1]; the author also says priority is unconfirmed.

significance.basis: It sharpens the known failure of polynomial Lyapunov converses to a sharp boundary for one two-parameter family and shows degree blow-up. The scope is narrow (single harmonic family) and the paper itself says dynamical stability is unaffected.

reproducibility.basis: The proofs are self-contained and checkable by hand. The numerics (2048-factor product, Toeplitz relaxations) are described only in summary, and no code, data or formal proof is supplied. The paper admits the quantile construction has no certified numerics.

summary: The manuscript classifies, for the stable cubic family of Liu-Fitzsimmons (r'=r^3(-a+b cos2θ), θ'=r^2), when polynomial or local analytic Lyapunov certificates exist: exactly when |b|^{2/3}<1+a^{2/3}. Necessity uses a moment pairing with an explicit square-root test function. Sufficiency uses a limiting harmonic pair, Poisson smoothing and quantile approximation, with an explicit O(delta^{-3}) degree bound. Extensions cover single even harmonics and an SOS corollary. I found no error on hand re-derivation of the main steps; remaining concerns are terse boundary-regularity details and unverified priority.
strengths: Sharp iff statement covering weak, strict, product-of-quadratics and local analytic certificates, including exclusion of the boundary.
Necessity argument is short and I re-derived it; the optimisation over c gives the stated threshold and is consistent with the earlier 2(a+1) obstruction (threshold is below it).
Explicit degree bound with checkable constants, and honest statements of limits and open questions.
Frank disclosure of AI assistance and of the lack of blind, human or formal verification.
weaknesses: Boundary behaviour of h_c at the exceptional points (continuity, minimum principle) is stated rather than carefully proved.
Corollary 6 for general k, omega and the d sin2θ perturbation are proved by 'replace z by z^k' remarks.
No matching lower degree bound, so degree divergence is qualitative only.
Novelty relies on one very recent preprint; no independent verification or formal check of this manuscript.
The numerical section is anecdotal and not reproducible from the text alone.
potential_errors: Eq. (9): the sigma factor from (8) (b*sigma*c/s) is absorbed in the limit; fine, but the intermediate inequality with sigma is not written out.
Section 6: the claim that p_m is positive definite uses the lowest-order term only; it should say explicitly that L_f P_m may vanish identically (still covered by the inequality).
Lemma 2 invokes Fejer-Riesz 'in the form used in [1]'; I did not check that source's exact statement.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact threshold |b|^{2/3}<1+a^{2/3} for polynomial and local analytic Lyapunov certificates, with equality excluded.
Boundary limiting harmonic pair via the explicit square-root function f_c and its Poisson-smoothed approximation giving an O(delta^{-3}) degree bound.
